title: A three-manifold without conjugate points or nonpositive curvature
manuscript: A Three-Manifold Without Conjugate Points and Without a Nonpositively Curved Metric (OpenAI, September 24, 2026)
analyst_role: family analyst (paper + Lean); reasoning trace: none for this family
base_library_L: Mathlib d13f23b + references.bib of this manuscript (8 entries: BridsonHaefliger1999, BurnsMatveev2021, Gulliver1975, IvanovKapovitch2014, Leeb1995, KapovichLeeb1996, Milnor1963, Bonahon2009)

main_statement.paraphrase: Some closed orientable 3-manifold (a two-piece graph manifold made of two copies of (punctured torus) x S^1, glued by h2=h1+f1, f2=h1) carries a smooth metric with no conjugate points, yet carries no nonpositively curved metric. This answers negatively, already in dimension 3, the question (Ivanov-Kapovitch Q1.1/Q8.1; Burns-Matveev Q4.1.2) whether a closed manifold without conjugate points must admit a nonpositively curved metric.

stronger_claims_in_paper.paraphrase: pi_1(M) admits no proper cocompact isometric action on a nonempty proper CAT(0) space (Thm no-cat0-action).
M admits no locally CAT(0) length metric inducing its topology (Cor no-local-cat0).
M admits no metric without focal points (via IvanovKapovitch2014 Thm 7.1, cited).

comparator.readable: There is a compact, connected, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth (C^infinity) 3-manifold with an oriented atlas, a smooth Riemannian metric g with no conjugate points, and no smooth Riemannian metric with nonpositive sectional curvature. Curvature and Christoffel symbols are defined chart-wise from the metric matrix; NPC means g(R(u,v)v,u)<=0 for all u,v in every atlas chart; NoConjugatePoints quantifies over every open interval U, every geodesic on U (including constant and non-unit-speed ones) and every chart-wise smooth Jacobi field on U vanishing at two distinct times, concluding that J vanishes on U.

A.label: A2

evidence.quote: There exists a closed connected orientable smooth three-manifold $M$ with a $C^\infty$ Riemannian metric without conjugate points, such that $M$ admits no $C^\infty$ Riemannian metric

A.note: A counterexample (exists M). Its second conjunct is an impossibility statement (no NPC metric on M), proved by a group-theoretic obstruction; the first conjunct is a construction. The comparator is the same exists-statement.

B.label: B2

flags.full_only_with_prior_results_detail: Self-contained modulo standard cited theorems (flat torus theorem and cyclic minset theorem of Bridson-Haefliger, metric Cartan-Hadamard, Milnor's index-form framework). The obstruction is Leeb's example, re-proved. No prior model output used.
flags.adds_corollaries_detail: The same M has no proper cocompact CAT(0) action of pi_1, no locally CAT(0) metric, and (via IK Thm 7.1) no metric without focal points. It also answers Burns-Matveev Question 4.1.2 in dimension three.
flags.does_not_address: Ivanov-Kapovitch Question 8.2 (two copies of Sigma x S^1 glued by A in SL(2,Z) with |tr A|>2). With the natural (boundary, fibre) bases and an orientation correction, the paper's gluing [[1,1],[1,0]] (det -1) has |trace| = 1, so it is a different gluing; the paper does not claim to settle Q8.2, though its intro sentence 'ask about gluings of two punctured-torus products' could be misread that way.

evidence.quote: We give a negative answer in dimension three, using a metric on a two-piece graph manifold whose topology obstructs nonpositive curvature.

B.note: The posed problem is a yes/no question (IK Q1.1/Q8.1 'Does every closed Riemannian manifold without conjugate points admit a metric of nonpositive curvature?'). Answering 'no' with a counterexample is B2. IK expected 'probably no' in general but allowed that dimension 3 might be different.

route_differences_vs_paper: No flat torus theorem: the obstruction is a CN-space 'cyclic shear' lemma using only common minimum points, axes and axis shifts (Convexity.lean:696).
Smooth Cartan-Hadamard, Gauss lemma and an NPC Jacobi-norm lower bound are re-proved from scratch to get the CN universal-cover metric (Distance.lean, Geodesics.lean, Continuation.lean).

Nontriviality of the fibre classes is proved with the constructed no-conjugate-points metric (fibres are closed geodesics, hence essential), not with van Kampen; so the non-NPC half depends on the whole metric construction.
The H_0^1 / Riesz dual-norm argument (S(q,r)) is replaced by an explicit pointwise quadratic and integration by parts (DirectTurning).
Passages are taken inside a compact window containing the field's support, so half-infinite passages are replaced by 'truncated returns' with vanishing field at the window edge.
The punctured torus is H/<phi,psi,-1> in SL(2,Z) with torsion-freeness by reductions mod 2 and mod 3; the neck sits in the cusp collar 2<Im z<8 with flip x->16/x and a radial reparametrisation.

eureka_candidates.for: Nothing in L or the goal resembles a free-endpoint nonnegativity statement for the normal index along every returning geodesic segment through a positively curved neck, uniform in duration and incidence. It needs three coordinated insights: the boundary term controls only the e-component of the endpoint change; the mixed coefficient S(p,e) must be within O(delta|p1|) of L p1 (not O(delta|p|)); and a strict timing margin beta<1 for excursions leaving the end collar. The paper itself flags it as what 'permits one metric to handle every complete geodesic'.
eureka_candidates.against: Each step is elementary (Cauchy-Schwarz, Schur complement, convexity), and once P19/P20/P24 are set up the target inequality is forced; an expert may see it as routine bookkeeping. It is a one-off device for this metric, so it would fail the downstream speedup test.

correctness_audit.verdict: No gap found. I re-derived the key computations by hand (below). The Lean development proves the comparator statement with a clean trust surface (not built here), and the comparator definitions are faithful. Confidence in correctness is high.
checked: End germs: for t<=1/3, A(1-t)=A(1), so P=diag(1+delta A(t), b); in frame T2=(e2+eps e1, e1), T2^{-1}H=e1 and T2^{-1}e1=e2 give diag(d2,b). Matches (cometric.tex:72-75).
a(0)=e^{-3/2} and a(1/8)/a(0)=exp(-24/13+3/2)=exp(-9/26), as claimed; Lean aZero=exp(-3/2), beta identical.
Coordinate energy: with Q'=-QP'Q, Q''=2QP'QP'Q-QP''Q and xdot=Pp, the coordinate second variation equals int(wdot^2+|zdot-wP'p|_Q^2 - F''w^2/2).
Boundary term: Gamma^t_ij=-Q'_ij/2 and Q'(0)=-kappa e1e1^T give Gamma(V,V)=(kappa/2)z1^2 d_tau; signs at entry (taudot>0, added) and exit (taudot<0, subtracted) are both nonnegative.
Turning identity: q(0)=p^T z(0) when w(0)=0; int qdot^2=(p^T Delta z)^2/L for affine q; (a^2+b^2)>=(b-a)^2/2 gives mu=kappa v0/4.
Timing: vddot=-F''v/2>=0 on the first half, chord bound gives int v^2<=Lv0^2/3; int F'=4v0 split over the middle and outer halves gives 4v0<=beta kappa p1^2 L.

S-bounds: Phi_p(w)=2 int v wdot gives S(p,p)<=L+3int v^2<=L(1+v0^2); domination gives ||Phi_e||^2<=2C0 delta L; D(t)=P'(0)-P'(t)>=0 and PSD Cauchy-Schwarz give |e^T P' p|<=(a(0)+sqrt(2C0 a(0))) delta|p1|.

Final inequality: L mu>=r/beta, x/(1+C_e x) increasing, r<=a(0)delta, and the delta-choice give S(p,e)^2/(S(e,e)+1/mu)>=Lv0^2, so the Schur complement is <=L. Lean's SmallParameter is the same delta-choice.

Obstruction: tau_i(h_i)=0 and Pythagoras on a common flat give orthogonality; v(h2)=u+v, v(f2)=u gives |u|^2=0. Lean's actual_loop_relations encode f2=h1 and h2=h1 f1 (FundamentalGroup.lean:491-519), matching (topology.tex:22-24).

consistency_checks_passed: Green's theorem (total scalar curvature <=0 for compact manifolds without conjugate points): satisfied, since the hyperbolic cores dominate.
IK centralizer splitting: C(f_1) contains G_1=F_2 x Z, which splits. Dibble 2018 (abelian subgroups are Z^k, solvable subgroups Bieberbach): satisfied by a graph-manifold group.
IK Thm 7.1 forces focal points on M; the metric does have them (positive curvature in the neck middle), consistent.

Free-endpoint I^perp_J>=0 with parallel normal V means the integral of K(V,T) along each passage is <=0; this is compatible with positive curvature being met only briefly with compensating negative curvature near the ends of each excursion.
